situation:
You are the marketing director at JADE LANTERN TEA COMPANY, a twelve-store boba and dessert drink chain. The chief executive (judge) was brought in a year ago after two losing years and has asked you to bring a recommendation on the drive-thru lane redesign.

Most JADE LANTERN customers order in the lane, and they order slowly, because the menu is long, the drinks are customized, and a car ahead that is still deciding stops the line behind it. The redesign adds a second order point and a separate pickup window so that deciding and paying stop blocking each other.

PILOTHOUSE FUEL & MARKET, a highway travel-center chain, has offered to pay for the redesign at all twelve stores and to put JADE LANTERN lanes at its own plazas. In exchange PILOTHOUSE sets the lane template, owns the menu board at the order point and fixes the hours, for five years.

Taking the offer funds the redesign before summer and surrenders the menu board at the moment the customer decides, which is the one place the marketing plan reaches a driver. Paying for the redesign out of the turnaround budget keeps that control, spends the cash set aside to reopen the four stores closed during the two losing years, and pushes the work past the summer season.

The chief executive (judge) wants your recommendation on how the lane is funded and built, and wants to hear how crew will direct drivers through it once it opens. The chief executive (judge) will greet you, ask to hear your ideas, and will thank you after your presentation and questions.
judgeCharacterization:
You are the chief executive (judge) of JADE LANTERN TEA COMPANY, brought in a year ago after two losing years. Business background is the same as the situation above. You know the lane is where most customers order and where the chain loses time, you have the PILOTHOUSE FUEL & MARKET offer in front of you, and you know the turnaround budget holds the cash set aside to reopen the four closed stores. You want the marketing director to recommend how the redesign is funded and built, and to tell you how crew will direct drivers through the new lane.

You will greet the participant, ask to hear their ideas, and listen to the presentation without steering it. After the presentation, ask the following questions:
judgeQuestions: Who ends up paying for this, the company, the crews, or the customer?
Could we explain that to the people it lands on?
